events.reader_segment: A couple aged 26 or over at the same address who expect to visit historic places, gardens or countryside together
events.promise: Help the reader judge membership against their own planned visits, eligibility and appetite for an annually renewing commitment, without claiming that it will save them money.
events.arc: One self-contained decision email moves the reader from a general interest in membership to a practical comparison of their plans, joint-membership terms and the benefits they would actually use.

emails.job: Prompt the reader to compare joint membership with their own planned visits and review the applicable options and conditions.
emails.single_idea: Joint membership is worth considering through a simple fit check: whether both adults meet its household and age rules, whether their planned visits would make use of entry to more than 500 places, and whether its payment and renewal terms suit them.
emails.objection: We may not visit often enough for membership to feel worth the price.
must_not_say: That any number of visits will make membership worthwhile
That membership guarantees savings or is cheaper than individual admission
Any local place, event, opening time or location-specific access detail
That monthly payments reduce the annual cost or remove the commitment
That Direct Debit is a one-year trial, can be cancelled in a particular way or comes with a renewal reminder
Any benefit, exception, price or condition not supported by the imported membership page
That this is a new offer or launch
Customer testimonials, usage claims or measurable results
emails.felt_need: We have historic places and outdoor visits in mind, but we want to know whether membership fits how we are likely to visit before committing.
emails.status_quo: They are comparing membership with arranging their planned visits individually.
emails.mechanism: Give the reader concrete terms to judge: joint membership covers two adults aged 26 or over living at the same address and costs £168 a year or 12 monthly payments of £14; membership includes free entry to more than 500 places in the National Trust's care; Direct Debit renews automatically after one year.
emails.call_to_action: Review the membership options and conditions
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether joint membership's eligibility, price, included entry and renewal arrangement fit their planned visits.
emails.next_step_value: The membership page lets them review the available options and check the stated joint-membership terms, included entry and Direct Debit renewal condition.
emails.next_step_limit: It does not establish a personal break-even point or guarantee savings because no individual admission-price comparison or visit-frequency calculation is supplied.

alternative_arguments.single_idea: Membership can be considered not only as access to places, but as a way to support their continued care while receiving practical visiting benefits.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: We want our days out to support places we value, but we still need to understand what membership includes.
alternative_arguments.status_quo: They may otherwise pay for visits individually or support conservation separately.
alternative_arguments.why_it_fails: The supplied evidence does not establish whether paying per visit or donating separately would be better for this couple.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: Every penny from membership goes towards looking after nature, beauty and history, while members receive free entry to more than 500 places and free parking at most National Trust car parks.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: membership is mainly another way to pay for days out. After: it combines visiting benefits with support for the care of nature, beauty and history, although the reader must still judge whether the terms fit.
must_not_say: That membership is better than paying for individual visits or donating directly
That parking is free at every National Trust car park
Customer stories, popularity claims or measurable conservation outcomes
alternative_arguments.objection: I would rather pay only when I visit or donate directly than commit to membership.
alternative_arguments.call_to_action: Review the membership options and conditions
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether the combination of visiting benefits and support for places in the National Trust's care suits how they want to visit and contribute.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The membership page lets them review the stated benefits alongside the available membership choices and their conditions.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: The page evidence supplied does not compare membership with individual admission costs or direct donations, so it cannot determine which route is financially better for this reader.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Frame membership as both visiting and looking after places, using restrained language rather than an emotional appeal or savings claim.

events.subject: Does joint membership fit your plans?
events.preview_text: Check the eligibility, price, included entry and renewal terms.
events.body:
National Trust joint membership gives two adults free entry to more than 500 places in our care. Your membership also supports our work looking after nature, beauty and history.

Joint membership covers two adults aged 26 or over who live at the same address. It costs **£168 a year** or 12 monthly payments of £14.

If you’re wondering whether you’ll visit often enough, compare those terms with the places and visits you have in mind. The useful question is whether the included entry fits your own plans.

If you choose Direct Debit, your membership automatically renews after one year. The membership page sets out the available options and conditions, so you can check the details before deciding.

Review membership options and conditions

– the National Trust team

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "Visit places and help care for them"
events.subject: Visit places and help care for them
events.preview_text: Compare the visiting benefits with your plans and the membership conditions.
events.body:
National Trust membership brings visits and support for places in our care together. Every penny from membership goes towards looking after nature, beauty and history – for everyone, for ever.

Membership includes free entry to over 500 places in our care, plus free parking at most National Trust car parks. These benefits may be useful if you expect to explore historic places, gardens or countryside together.

Paying for individual visits or donating separately may still suit you. The membership page does not decide which route is better, but it can help you compare what membership includes with the visits you have in mind.

If you are considering joint membership, check the available choices and conditions before deciding whether an annual commitment fits.

Review membership options and conditions
